comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027; adopted OER and exact annual guide, checked 2026-10-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized target merges English Communication Science and Dutch Communicatiewetenschap registrations. The adopted OER first lists the English route; both are language versions of the same subject. Ten 6-EC units fill Year 1; eight 6-EC named courses and two restricted Social Sciences for Society choice slots fill Year 2. Year 3 has 30 EC of genuinely open approved electives, Current Media Challenges (6), Philosophy of Science (6) and an 18-EC empirical bachelor thesis. Zero-credit mentorship is excluded. Choice menus are represented as slots, not accumulated options. The English-language 2026–2027 route totals 180 EC: ten 6 EC compulsory units in Year 1; eight 6 EC prescribed units and two 6 EC restricted Social Sciences for Society choices in Year 2; and 30 EC open study, 6 EC Current Media Challenges, 6 EC Philosophy of Science and an 18 EC thesis in Year 3. Choice slots represent one option from each stated menu. Thesis entry requires a pass in Quantitative Research Methodology and 90 EC from Years 1–2. Empirical research is conducted in small groups, with individual assignments and thesis reporting: assignments A–D contribute 40%, and the individual thesis 60% (30% supervisor, 30% second reader); the assignment average and both thesis assessments must be sufficient. Weekly team meetings and supervision in periods 5–6 are mandatory. Topic preferences are submitted in mid-March after Canvas instructions in early March; supervisors provide the topics and allocate students. Course and component registration remains required. Zero-credit Year-3 mentorship requires attendance at group and individual meetings and must be completed before the thesis grade is awarded. A compulsory language diagnostic and any required refresher/remedial pass are conditions for the Project 1 grade, without extra EC. Practical/tutorial attendance is compulsory. BSA ordinarily requires 42 first-year EC; a language-test deferral can apply at 36 EC including the relevant course. Individual open choices require prior board approval and at least 12 EC at level 300; level 100 is excluded except an approved 6 EC prerequisite in a coherent package. Listed faculty electives and university/listed minors have approval exemptions; overlapping Sociology-minor credit requires replacement. Internships need coordinator approval. Earlier-cohort substitutions and optional outcomes are not extra requirements.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Communication Science studies how media and messages influence people, organizations and public life. This comparison uses its English-language route, with theoretical and empirical methods courses, four communication projects and a final empirical thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers two qualified approaches built from rhetorical communication, persuasion, media and audience analysis, social psychology, qualitative inquiry, research design, statistics and data analysis. The primary adds organizational and market research; the second emphasizes interpretation and public debate. These course contributions respond to communication-science questions, but do not reproduce VU’s four structured projects, specialist media-effects and health-campaign training, computational media/LLM sequence or empirical thesis. Creative Communication Laboratory is principally poetic and experimental expression, not a campaign project. Rhetoric in Action involves school-based speaking practice conducted mainly in Dutch; participants must check the practical language conditions. Neither composition establishes course equivalence, a professional qualification or automatic master’s eligibility.
